fixes.explanation: That's what he picks up. The lament says, “After learning to tear his prey…” and then it tells where that leads. Some folks learn to cook. This young lion learned something a lot rougher. Keep your eye on him, friend, because the nations are paying attention too.
No crown in this verse, friend. When the nations heard of him, he was trapped in their pit. After that, hooks led him away to the land of Egypt. A pit and hooks are a long way from a coronation.

This lion doesn't get to push anybody out. The lament says, “When the nations heard of him, he was trapped in their pit.” Nothing in the verse has him driving anyone from their land. Instead, hooks led him away to the land of Egypt, baker.

That's the word, baker. The lament says, “He broke down their strongholds and devastated their cities.” Strongholds are fortified places, and he breaks them down. This is a lion who doesn't knock before he enters. And the whole land notices.

Yes, baker. The lament says, “With hooks they caged him and brought him to the king of Babylon.” So this time it's the king of Babylon, not Egypt like the first cub. Hooks and a cage. It's a rough ride for a lion.

Moab isn't in this verse, friend. The text says the nations caged him with hooks and brought him to the king of Babylon. The king of Babylon is the name to remember here. Then the verse says his roar was heard no longer on the mountains of Israel.

Assyria isn't named here, baker. The lament says, “With hooks they caged him and brought him to the king of Babylon.” That's the king the text gives. Keep him in your pocket, because the verse says they brought him into captivity.

That's it, baker. The lament says the vine was uprooted in fury and cast down to the ground, and “…the east wind dried up its fruit.” So the wind is what dries the fruit. It's like a batch left on the counter with the oven off and the window open all week. No one's eating that one.
Gathering isn't in this verse, baker. The lament says the vine was uprooted in fury and cast down to the ground. Then “…the east wind dried up its fruit.” The wind is the one doing the work here.

The vineyard wall never shows up here, friend. The lament says fire has gone out from the main branch and devoured its fruit. The fire starts on the vine itself. Then the verse closes by saying no strong branch remains fit for a ruler's scepter.
